title: The platform you will build

beats.say: Over this program you build one data platform for Meridian, a ride-hailing and food delivery company. Every module adds one layer while the rest keeps running.

show.sub: built a layer at a time

beats.say: Rider and driver apps send events to Kafka. Orders change in Postgres, and Debezium captures each change. Spark processes both, in batch and in streams, into Iceberg tables on object storage.
dbt turns those tables into clean models that Trino, Snowflake and Databricks serve to dashboards. Airflow schedules every step, and an on-call agent reads failures and reports them.

show.note: Airflow schedules it; an agent watches it

check.q: Which tool captures every change in the Postgres orders table?
check.why: Debezium reads the database log and turns each insert, update and delete into an event.

sec: From a platform to a data foundation
title: From a platform to a foundation

beats.say: A platform that one engineer runs is not yet a foundation a company can build on. Other teams need to use it without asking you every time.

show.sub: other teams use it without you

beats.say: Three things make the difference. Golden paths: a template that creates a new pipeline in minutes. Governance: every dataset has an owner, a class like personal or public, and a rule for who may read it and how long it is kept.
And the platform run as a product: onboarding, docs, published service levels, and showing each team what it costs. Modules O1 to O5 teach this.

opts: A ready-made template that sets up a new pipeline the approved way
check.why: It makes the right way the easy way: tests, logging and CI come with the template.
